At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple marketed the feature as the final step to "completely ditch your physical wallet."

The following states will be adding support for Apple Wallet driver's license feature...

Apple Wallet ID Support

In the five years since Apple announced this feature, support has gradually expanded across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add their driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can view the complete list here:

Where will this feature roll out next? Here's what we know so far.

The following seven states have confirmed work on Apple Wallet driver's license support, been listed by Apple as partners, or have appeared in Apple code:

  • Kentucky (launching in "summer" 2026)
  • North Carolina (launching in early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in development, launch timing TBD)
  • Utah (in development, launch timing TBD)
  • Virginia (in development, launch timing TBD)
  • Connecticut (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)
  • Mississippi (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)

Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking mobile driver's license support rollouts across the country. The following states have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or research, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

It's important to note that progress varies significantly from state to state. Even if a state is exploring or developing digital ID support, that doesn't necessarily mean it will eventually launch — let alone make its way to Apple Wallet.

Wrap-up

As you can see, the rollout of Apple Wallet driver's license support across the United States remains quite uneven.

However, even if your state doesn't yet support digital IDs in Apple Wallet, you don't have to wait.

Apple launched a new Digital ID feature last year powered by U.S. passports. While it's not your driver's license, it does allow you to use your iPhone at TSA security checkpoints at more than 250 airports nationwide.

Do you have your ID or driver's license stored in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Let us know in the comments.
